Subject: Workload temporal sharding & sizing questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this — we're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production rollout and want to validate whether temporal sharding (splitting traffic by time windows / cold-start tolerant lanes) will help us hit latency and cost goals. A few quick details about our setup:
- Service: conversational search + long-form summarization (combined routing)
- Typical traffic: daily steady-state with short ~90s burst windows tied to user sessions
- Models: mixture of an instruction-tuned Llama variant and a summarization finetune (we'll share exact names)

To size properly, could you confirm what you need from us? Off the top of my head: average & peak RPS, concurrency targets, prompt & response token distributions, tolerance for quantization, and whether sharding by time-of-day is something Redwood recommends for Dedicated.

I'll send a small sample CSV (minute-level traffic for a 48h window) — attaching the ProdOps contact list and will drop the CSV in a follow-up.

Goal: p95 end-to-end generation <= 200ms for the search path; summarization can be p95 <= 800ms. Also curious how caching/prefix batching would interact with a temporal-sharded fleet.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
ProdOps
Helium AI

Tessa — quick technical notes to seed the call. I sketched a few options and attached a short diagram (shard-mapping-sketch.png). High level:

Option A — Time-window shards (simple):
- Create three Dedicated pools: steady-state (low-latency tiny batch), burst pool (higher concurrency, bigger batch windows), and cold lane (spin-up models for rare long-running summaries).
- Use auto-scaling with short warm-up targets; prefer pre-warmed model replicas for the steady stage.
- Expected concurrency per GPU: ~10-20 gen sessions on H100 (fp16) for 1k tokens/session at 150ms target. If use int8 we can push concurrency higher but watch quality regressions.

Option B — Route-by-QL (quality lane):
- Route sensitive summarization to larger-memory SKUs (A100x, pinned replicas) and route search to quantized variants for cost efficiency.

Batching & KV cache notes:
- If prompts are highly similar (search prefixes), prefix caching will dramatically reduce per-token cost and improve p95.
- Continuous batching window of 10-20ms balances latency and throughput in our runtime; for p95=200ms targets keep batching windows <=20ms for search paths.

Data we need to run accurate GPU counts:
- 48h minute-level CSV (you mentioned sending)
- Token distributions broken into 0-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513+ bins (affects inferred compute per-request)

Rough back-of-envelope: for mixed workload with 220 RPS average and 3.5k1s peak bursts, plan for a hot steady pool sized for ~300 RPS and a burst pool with capacity to absorb the remaining peak for 60s windows. That maps to ~6-8 H100 equivalents for steady and 10-12 for burst buffer (very rough — will refine with real CSV).

Attachment: shard-mapping-sketch.png (diagram).
